paper.title_en: Entanglement Harvesting Landscapes: A Common Computational Framework
paper.abstract_en: Entanglement harvesting provides an operational means of probing nonlocal correlations of quantum fields through localized detector-field interactions. Although studied in diverse spacetime backgrounds and quantum field states, existing studies largely focus on individual detector configurations. Here, we develop a unified perturbative framework for localized Unruh-DeWitt detectors, applicable to different detector trajectories and quantum field states through the corresponding Wightman function. Expressing detector responses in dimensionless variables and analytically reducing the perturbative integrals to numerically efficient representations enables systematic exploration of multidimensional harvesting landscapes and phase boundaries. We investigate inertial detectors in the Minkowski vacuum, thermal field states, and uniformly accelerated detectors undergoing Born-rigid motion. In the latter case, the detectors have different proper accelerations and different Unruh temperatures, leading to unequal local excitation probabilities. The harvested entanglement is evaluated by accounting for both local detector responses and the nonlocal exchange amplitude. Increasing temperature enhances the detector excitation probability while generally suppressing the magnitude of the nonlocal exchange amplitude. Consequently, within the perturbative Gaussian-switching framework and over the parameter range investigated, thermal effects suppress harvested entanglement and reduce the spatial extent of the harvesting region. The resulting landscapes provide a global characterization of detector-field interactions and demonstrate how temperature and observer motion reshape the competition between local detector noise and nonlocal field correlations. This framework provides an extensible methodology for investigating entanglement harvesting across relativistic quantum systems.
